evidence: Ser. ap. Diom. p. 516 P.: graphidem date (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A drawing pencil in a fragment quoted by Diomedes; in Vitruvius and Pliny it is drawing itself (Lewis & Short). Rarer than Traupman’s graphium, classically a stylus.

phrases.latin: Graphium cape et nōmen tuum scrībe.
phrases.english: Take a pencil and write your name.

phrases.latin: Graphium rēctē tenē: sīc, tribus digitīs.
phrases.english: Hold the pencil properly: like this, with three fingers.

phrases.latin: Puerī ad praescrīptum discunt; digitī illōrum tenentur et aliēnā manū per litterārum simulācra dūcuntur
phrases.english: Children learn by copying a model; their fingers are held and guided by another’s hand along the shapes of the letters

phrases.latin: neque egēbit adjūtōriō manum suam manū super impositā regentis
phrases.english: and he will not need the help of someone guiding his hand with a hand laid over it

phrases.latin: Ubi sunt graphia colōrāta? — In thēcā.
phrases.english: Where are the coloured pencils? — In the pencil case.

sources: Lewis & Short: graphium · Lewis & Short: plumbum · Lewis & Short: coloratus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 30, 338.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. pen: pencil.
